patch.value: GH-1663: nested get --fields projections pad unrequested sibling collections with empty arrays (linked.files emits tests: [] and docs: [] for populated collections) and claim_state.claimed expands to the whole group

GitHub issue #1663 (reported 2026-11-04 against 2026.11.4 from an agent-UX audit). Reproduced 2026-11-05 on the installed 2026.11.4 CLI in a sandbox tracker whose one claimed Task has exactly one linked file, one linked test and one linked doc. pm get <id> --fields id,linked.files,claim_state.claimed --json returns linked with files holding the one file but tests: [] and docs: [], although both collections are populated, and pm get <id> --fields linked.tests --json likewise returns files: [] and docs: []. claim_state.claimed returns the whole claim_state group (claimed, assignee, last_claim, last_release). The omission_receipt in both responses reports has_omissions false, so nothing tells the caller that the empty siblings were not requested. The reporter reproduced it through the public SDK with client.get(id, {fields: 'id,linked.files,claim_state.claimed'}). Expected: an unrequested sibling under a nested path is omitted or explicitly marked as not requested, a genuinely requested empty collection still renders as [], and a nested claim_state leaf selects that leaf, or the contract documents that it expands to the group. Why it matters for agents: agents keep several narrow reads as durable context, and an empty tests or docs array reads as evidence of absence, which can trigger duplicate linking or a false claim that verification is missing. Relation to closed work: pm-4fwgaz (GH-1033) made requested empty collections render as [], and its AC3 requires typed receipts to distinguish absent, empty, omitted and inapplicable groups, which a has_omissions false receipt beside padded siblings does not do. pm-b1w8vr AC1 made an absent key mean not carried and never empty, and this is the inverse failure: an empty key that means not carried. pm-cyrfjq fixed the same zero-fill class for mode-paired envelopes. Duplicate check: searched nested fields, linked projection, claim_state projection, absent versus empty and zero-fill across all statuses, and no open item owns this.

pm get --fields with a nested path such as linked.files or linked.tests emits only the requested child keys of that group, or marks each unrequested sibling explicitly as not requested, and never renders an unrequested populated collection as an empty array, in CLI JSON, TOON, SDK and MCP; A requested collection that is genuinely empty still renders as an empty array, so requested-empty and unrequested stay distinguishable, proven by a spec over an item with both populated and empty collections; omission_receipt reports the unrequested siblings of a nested projection as omitted, each with a restore_with, instead of has_omissions false; claim_state.claimed returns only the claimed leaf, or the projection contract and get help state that nested claim_state paths expand to the whole group and the receipt says so; Negative control: reintroducing the parent-group default padding fails the spec

In a fresh tracker, create and claim one Task, link one file, one doc and one test. pm get <id> --fields id,linked.files,claim_state.claimed --json and pm get <id> --fields linked.tests --json show empty sibling arrays and has_omissions false
A nested projection returns only what was requested, or marks the rest as not requested, so an empty collection always means empty

--fields linked.files returns tests: [] and docs: [] for populated collections, linked.tests returns files: [] and docs: [], and claim_state.claimed returns the full group, all with has_omissions false

value.text:
Re-reproduced 2026-11-06 on main a14511d0f (the 2026.11.5 cut plus the artifact-preflight fix) in a one-item sandbox with one linked file, doc and test.

pm get <id> --fields id,linked.files,claim_state.claimed --json returns linked.files with the file, but tests: [] and docs: []. claim_state comes back whole (claimed, assignee, last_claim, last_release), and omission_receipt reports has_omissions false. --fields linked.tests behaves the same: files: [] and docs: [].

Source: attachGetLinked in src/sdk/query/get.ts deliberately keeps the linked envelope's stable three-group shape, filling unselected groups with [] (its docstring says so). resolveGetReceipt in src/sdk/output-projection.ts counts a linked group as included only when it is non-empty, so a padded placeholder is never reported as omitted. shouldIncludeGetField treats any claim_state.* selector as the whole group (fieldsIncludeRoot).

Design constraint for the fix: GetResult.linked declares files, tests and docs as required arrays. Omitting unrequested siblings therefore changes the public SDK type and needs sdk:surface:update --acknowledge-breaking plus migration notes. The non-breaking alternative keeps the shape but records each padded sibling in omission_receipt with restore_with --fields linked.<group>, plus an explicit per-group not-requested marker. Either way, a requested empty group must still render as [] and stay distinguishable.

Re-reproduced 2026-11-06 on main a14511d0f (the 2026.11.5 cut plus the artifact-preflight fix) in a one-item sandbox with one linked file, doc and test.

pm get <id> --fields id,linked.files,claim_state.claimed --json returns linked.files with the file, but tests: [] and docs: []. claim_state comes back whole (claimed, assignee, last_claim, last_release), and omission_receipt reports has_omissions false. --fields linked.tests behaves the same: files: [] and docs: [].

Source: attachGetLinked in src/sdk/query/get.ts deliberately keeps the linked envelope's stable three-group shape, filling unselected groups with [] (its docstring says so). The receipt cannot report the padded siblings for a second reason. For explicit --fields selectors, runGet calls registerOutputMaterialFieldGroups with an empty set. resolveGetReceipt in src/sdk/output-projection.ts then filters its declared groups down to material groups or keys present on the projected owner, which drops the unrequested tests and docs groups before any inclusion check runs. Changing only the non-empty predicate in isGetFieldGroupIncluded therefore cannot report these omissions. The fix must also declare unrequested nested siblings as omittable groups for field projections. shouldIncludeGetField treats any claim_state.* selector as the whole group (fieldsIncludeRoot).

Design constraint for the fix: GetResult.linked declares files, tests and docs as required arrays. Omitting unrequested siblings therefore changes the public SDK type and needs sdk:surface:update --acknowledge-breaking plus migration notes. The non-breaking alternative keeps the shape but records each padded sibling in omission_receipt with restore_with --fields linked.<group>, plus an explicit per-group not-requested marker. Either way, a requested empty group must still render as [] and stay distinguishable.
